name: Example: Finding the Acute Angle Between Two Vectors
problem: Find the acute angle between the vectors ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14046175/assets/5ed21f4bb536757026315cce838f4cc3028493adac2ff29d46a5b8cbdf11170b.png) and ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14046175/assets/8d813e104a708be37ba44b9448806f49ea21a16fe7f613314d2eeab2b59bbda2.png)
worked_solution:
Using the formula

$$
\cos\theta = \dfrac{\mathbf{v} \cdot \mathbf{w}}{\Vert\mathbf{v}\Vert \, \Vert \mathbf{w}\Vert},
$$

we have the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  & =\frac{{v}_{1}{w}_{1}+{v}_{2}{w}_{2}+{v}_{3}{w}_{3}+{v}_{4}{w}_{4}}{\sqrt{{v}_{1}^{2}+{v}_{2}^{2}+{v}_{3}^{2}+{v}_{4}^{2}}\,\sqrt{{w}_{1}^{2}+{w}_{2}^{2}+{w}_{3}^{2}+{w}_{4}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{(-1)\cdot (-2)+2\cdot 2+(-4)\cdot (-2)+(-2)\cdot 2}{\sqrt{(-1)^{2}+{2}^{2}+(-4)^{2}+(-2)^{2}}\,\sqrt{(-2)^{2}+{2}^{2}+(-2)^{2}+{2}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{10}{\sqrt{25}\cdot \sqrt{16}} \\  & =\frac{10}{5\cdot 4} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, 

$$
\theta=\arccos \left( \dfrac{1}{2} \right)=\dfrac{\pi}{3}.
$$
